axes.brief:
Competitive parliamentary elections, collegial executive government and frequent binding popular votes distribute authority widely. The Council is elected indirectly for four-year terms.
Focused six-question reassessment: Citizen constitutional initiatives and optional law-repeal referendums provide direct control, but the official federal explanation excludes introducing ordinary laws through popular initiative. The executive is collegial and elected indirectly; emergency ordinances and limited electoral exceptions remain legally bounded.
axes.counterEvidence:
No general federal recall or political no-confidence dismissal exists. Federal statutes cannot normally be struck down for unconstitutionality; some disabled adults remain excluded from voting.
